new_entities.name: Liothyronine added to levothyroxine in hypothyroidism
new_entities.description: Addition of liothyronine to levothyroxine replacement in adults with primary hypothyroidism, usually to address persistent symptoms despite biochemical euthyroidism.

new_entities.name: Well-being
new_entities.description: Overall subjective well-being, including mood, vitality, symptom burden, and patient-reported health status.

edges.effect_quant: Combination therapy remains preference-heavy but outcome-light. In a blinded meta-analysis of 7 RCTs with 348 participants, 46.2% preferred LT4+LT3, a rate not distinguishable from chance. A larger 141-patient trial showed increasing treatment preference with higher LT3 content, but a 46-patient JAMA trial found no advantage on hypothyroid-specific quality-of-life scores or cognitive testing.
edges.population: adults with treated primary hypothyroidism who remain dissatisfied or symptomatic on levothyroxine despite normal TSH
edges.mechanism: Adding liothyronine may improve tissue T3 availability in some patients whose symptom burden is not fully captured by serum TSH alone, potentially affecting mood, energy, and perceived well-being.
edges.summary: This edge is contested rather than clearly beneficial. Some patients prefer combination therapy and feel better on it, but average randomized-trial effects on well-being are inconsistent and often small or absent.
edges.caveats: Most trials are short, use different LT3 doses or T4:T3 ratios, and are not powered to identify biologically responsive subgroups. Preference does not necessarily equal objective outcome improvement, and T3-containing therapy brings greater complexity and potential overtreatment risk.

evidence.notes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Patient Preferences for Combination Thyroid Hormone Treatment for Hypothyroidism.

effect_quant.comparator: patients preferring LT4+LT3 over LT4 alone in blinded randomized trials

evidence.citation: AppelhofBC et al 2005 J Clin Endocrinol Metab
evidence.notes: Combined therapy with levothyroxine and liothyronine in two ratios, compared with levothyroxine monotherapy in primary hypothyroidism: a double-blind, randomized, controlled clinical trial.

effect_quant.comparator: preference for study medication in the LT4/LT3 5:1 group (52.2%) versus LT4-only group (29.2%)

evidence.notes: Combined levothyroxine plus liothyronine compared with levothyroxine alone in primary hypothyroidism: a randomized controlled trial.
